newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Aug M3 up 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Aug M3 up 8.7 pct.

text.p: Following are analysts' reactions to German August M3 money supply data which grew at an annualised rate of 8.7 percent compared with the fourth quarter 1995 average rate. In July the rate grew 8.6 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters on average expected a slowdown in annualised M3 growth to 8.0 percent.

Klaus Baader, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London told Reuters Financial Television: "The number is not a major catastrophe, but the process of rapid convergence toward the growth target (four to seven pct) has been interrupted. Reaching the target after this will be an uphill struggle.

Keith Edmonds, IBJ in London: The figure leaves "no room for the Bundesbank to cut the repo rate now. I expect the repo rate will be at three percent for some time. But the uptick in credit growth should only be a temporary factor."

Fritz Engelhard, Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich: "The strong growth was driven by the increase in short-term credit, but this should only be a short-term effect, and it will not be sustainable." Looking at the German debt market where Bund futures came off, Engelhard said, "I don't see a sustained dip (in Bunds)."
Engelhard added: "At the end of the day the bulls will be happier than the bears."

Soon after the M3 data was digested, the market began moving higher again after Ifo said the West German August business climate index was at 94.4 from 94.0 in July. The number laid to rest earlier market talk that it could be as high as 96.8.
